title: Continuous-flow protocol for photoredox-catalyzed multicomponent Petasis reaction
author: Oliva, Martens, et al.
materials: A complete list of reagents and equipment can be found in the “key resources table” and “materials and equipment”.

steps.title: Prepare reagent A solution
steps.instruction: In a 10 mL screw‑cap test tube, weigh 68 mg (0.6 mmol) cyclopentyl boronic acid and add 8 mg (0.007 mmol) [Ir{dF(CF3)ppy}2(dtbbpy)]PF₆, seal with a PTFE‑lined silicone septum, evacuate and refill with argon three times, then add 2 mL of a dry 3:1 DMF/MeCN mixture and finally add 24 µL (0.2 mmol) p‑anisaldehyde; ensure all solids are fully dissolved.

steps.title: Prepare reagent B solution
steps.instruction: In a second 10 mL screw‑cap test tube, add 27 µL (0.3 mmol) aniline with a Hamilton syringe, add 2 mL of a dry 3:1 DMF/MeCN mixture, seal with a PTFE‑lined silicone septum, place under argon, insert an outlet needle and degas the mixture for 5 min.

steps.title: Transfer reaction mixture to separatory funnel
steps.instruction: After the continuous‑flow reaction (≈1 h), pour the entire reaction mixture into a 250 mL separatory funnel, add 40 mL deionized water and 40 mL ethyl acetate (EtOAc), shake vigorously and allow the aqueous and organic layers to separate.

steps.title: Separate initial organic and aqueous layers
steps.instruction: Transfer the organic layer to one 200 mL Erlenmeyer flask and the aqueous layer to another 200 mL Erlenmeyer flask.

steps.title: Extract aqueous phase with EtOAc (three times)
steps.instruction: Return the aqueous phase to the separatory funnel, add 20 mL EtOAc, shake vigorously, allow phase separation, then transfer each layer to its respective Erlenmeyer flask; repeat this extraction two additional times (total three extractions).

substeps.instruction: Add 20 mL EtOAc to aqueous phase, shake, separate, transfer layers.

steps.title: Wash organic layer with water (three washes)
steps.instruction: Place the combined organic layer back into the separatory funnel, add 40 mL deionized water, shake vigorously, separate layers, discard the aqueous phase; repeat the water wash two more times (total three washes).

substeps.instruction: Add 40 mL water, shake, separate, discard aqueous phase.

steps.title: Brine wash of organic layer
steps.instruction: Add 40 mL brine (saturated NaCl solution) to the organic layer in the separatory funnel, shake, separate, and discard the aqueous brine phase.

steps.title: Acidify, filter, and collect crude product
steps.instruction: Transfer the washed organic layer to an Erlenmeyer flask, add solid NaHSO₄, gently swirl, then filter the suspension into a 100 mL round‑bottom flask.

steps.title: Remove solvent by rotary evaporation
steps.instruction: Evaporate the filtrate under reduced pressure at 44 °C and 235 mm Hg for approximately 15 min.

steps.title: Adsorb crude onto silica
steps.instruction: To the dried residue add 1 mL dichloromethane and 200 mg silica gel, swirl gently, then evaporate the solvent under vacuum at 38 °C and 800 mm Hg for about 10 min to afford a silica‑bound crude.

steps.title: Flash chromatography purification
steps.instruction: Pack a flash column (12 cm length, 2.5 cm diameter) with silica gel, load the silica‑bound crude, and elute with 200 mL of a 98:2 (v/v) heptane/ethyl acetate mixture; collect fractions containing product.

steps.title: Combine product fractions and concentrate
steps.instruction: Combine the pure product fractions and remove solvents under reduced pressure to afford the desired N‑(cyclopentyl(4‑methoxyphenyl)methyl)aniline.
